system.description:
3rd Level Clan Feature

The Kuru has spent generations training and mastering both their Miraigan’s ability to see the future and their unique ability to manifest their variant of Yin Release. This special variant of Yin Release allows them to emulate the properties of other Nature Releases without ever having to carry their affinities. If you cast a Jutsu with a Nature Release keyword, you can choose to have it lose that Nature Release keyword, and gain the Yin Release keyword as part of that Jutsu’s Casting. Otherwise, Jutsu you cast, can gain the Yin Release keyword as part of that jutsu’s casting. Effects that force a saving throw uses your highest jutsu save DC.

Yin Release. This jutsu’s damage type becomes Necrotic or Psychic. Additionally, if the jutsu could trigger any of the listed secondary effects found at the end of this section, that effect is replaced with the following; If the triggering jutsu forces a saving throw and the affected creature fails this saving throw, they are marked with a Yin-Seal until the end of your next turn. If the triggering jutsu doesn’t force a saving throw, then one of the affected creatures must make a Charisma saving throw vs the Jutsu’s save DC, being marked with a Yin-Seal until the end of your next turn on a failure.

No Nature Release: Inflicts a Condition

Earth Release: Creates difficult terrain or inflicts a Condition.

Wind Release: Swirl effect.

Fire Release: Flat damage modifier added as part of the damage calculation.

Water Release: Benefit for being near a source of Water.

Lightning Release: Overcharge effect.

Additionally, you have access to a deep pool of secret Kuru clan techniques known as Yin Arts, of which you know 1. You gain an additional selection at 7th and 15th levels.

Dual Sight

You learn to split your focus between today and tomorrow simultaneously. While your Miraigan is active, you can grant Fortune to two creature, rather than one when you use Prophesize. Though this causes you stress. You can now only use the Prophesize effect, once every other turn.

Prophetic Counter

You can now cycle between the future and the present between each step, strike and handsigns, but only while focusing on a single creature. While your Miraigan is active, you gain the Prophetic Counter ability.

Prophetic Counter. Once per turn, when a creature makes an attack targeting you and would score a hit, you can spend your Reaction and 2 Foresight to force them to remake their attack. If this would cause them to miss their attack, you can, as part of the same reaction take the Attack action targeting them.

Prophetic Weakness

You can now focus in on an enemies weaknesses and foresee their most critical openings. While your Miraigan is active, you gain the Prophetic Weakness ability

Prophetic Weakness. As a Bonus action you can spend 2 Foresight and select one creature you can see and foretell their weakness. Until the beginning of your next turn, they take +2 bonus damage from all sources. This increases to +4 at 7th level and +6 at 15th level.

Prophetic Teamwork

You can use your Miraigan to foresee the best possible way to work with your team, by viewing multiple scenarios and stitching together a plan. When an allied creature within 30 Feet of you would deal damage to a hostile creature, you can spend your Reaction and 2 Foresight to target another allied creature within 30 feet, that can target the same hostile creature. They gain the Prophetic Teamwork special action until the beginning of their next turn.

Prophetic Teamwork. This special action can only be used when it is not your turn. You can use any feature, jutsu or Attack that takes an Action, targeting a hostile creature that has taken damage this turn from an allied creature.

Yin Release – Veil of mystery

You can adjust the workings of your Yin Seal, allowing for you to share your visions with your foe, but only the ones you want to share. While a creature is marked with a Yin-Seal, you can spend 1 Foresight, targeting them to conjure a Misfortune which can only be used against them once before the end of your next turn. You can only maintain 1 Misfortune at a time. You can spend Misfortune to achieve one of the following;

Foretold Despair. subtract 1d4 from an attack roll, Skill check or saving throw they make.

Foretold Failure. To nullify any one jutsu based bonus, benefit or effect that applies to them.

Yin Release – Chains of Causality

You can adjust the workings of your Yin Seal, allowing for you to bind a vision of the future to your foe, making it their truth, their reality. While a creature is marked with a Yin-Seal, each time they make a Weapon attack or cast a jutsu, they suffer a -1 penalty to their AC for attacks you make against them, as each of these activities have been foreseen and it brings you closer to the destined strike you know to be true.

Beginning at 11th level, if your attack result would be 10 or higher than the AC of a Yin Sealed target, you treat that attack as a Critical hit.

Yin Release – Uncertain Future

You can adjust the workings of your Yin Seal, allowing for you to obfuscate the assumptions and plans they just had, blinding them to their own desires. While a creature is marked with a Yin-Seal, and they cast a jutsu or spends their Action, Bonus Action or Reaction while within 60 feet of a Kuru that can see them, that Kuru can spend their Reaction and spend 2 Foresight, forcing the Yin-Sealed creature to make a Charisma saving throw vs the Kuru’s highest jutsu save DC. On a failure, the Yin-Sealed creature must perform an alternative Action, Bonus Action, Reaction or Jutsu with the same casting time, or they lose the Action they spent as the ability to perform that action is temporarily sealed.

Black Fang – Yin Palm Strike

You focus Yin chakra into your palms and strike with claws like a wolves jaw. Once per turn, in place of an attack made as part of your Attack action, you can instead make a Yin Palm Strike.

Yin Palm Strike. Make an unarmed attack, dealing your [Unarmed Damage] on a hit, and forcing the affected creature to make a Charisma saving throw. On a failure, you inject Yin chakra into them, breaking their spiritual center, but marking them with a Yin-Seal.

Black Fang – Future Denial

You focus Yin chakra into your palms and strike at the temple of your foe. Once per turn, in place of an attack made as part of your Attack action, you can instead make a Denial Palm Strike.

Denial Palm Strike. Make an unarmed attack, dealing your [Unarmed Damage] on a hit, and forcing the affected creature to make a saving throw, using their associated jutsu modifier of the target discipline. On a failure, you inject Yin chakra into them, fragmenting their memories. Select one casting discipline between Ninjutsu, Taijutsu, Genjutsu and Bukijutsu; and one rank between E-Rank, D-Rank, C-Rank, B-Rank and A-Rank, for the next minute they cannot cast jutsu of the select discipline and rank. A creature affected by this remakes their saving throw at the end of each of their turns, ending the effect on a success.

Black Fang – Theft of Time

You focus Yin chakra into your palms and strike at where your foe believes they should be in time, replacing them with yourself and vice versa. Once per turn, in place of an attack made as part of an attack of opportunity, you can instead make a Time Theft Strike.

Time Theft Strike. Make an unarmed attack, dealing your [Unarmed Damage] on a hit, and forcing the affected creature to make a Charisma saving throw. On a failure, you use your Yin chakra affinity to rip their belief that they belong, and delay it. You switch places with them in initiative at the end of their current turn or next turn, whichever occurs first. If this initiative movement would cause you to miss taking a turn, you instead immediately take your turn, and initiative continues selecting the creature that would have gone normally. If this initiative movement would cause you to take an additional turn this round, you skip that turn in initiative. Hostile creatures that would miss their turn due to this feature, act at the end of the initiative round. A hostile creature that would gain an additional turn as a result of this swap loses that turn instead.
